slides.text:
A normal flag belongs to one command. A **persistent** flag belongs to a command and to everything below it, so a flag like `--verbose` is declared once on the root and works everywhere. You will share a flag, limit one to a branch of the tree and read an inherited value.

The snippet is pseudo code.
slides.code:
root   --verbose   (persistent)
  serve   accepts --verbose
  db      accepts --verbose
    migrate   accepts --verbose

slides.text: The method that owns the flag decides who accepts it: **`Flags()`** is for the command alone, **`PersistentFlags()`** is for the command and all its descendants. The flag can be written before or after the subcommand name.

exercises.title: A flag every command shares
exercises.guide: Register a flag on the root so its subcommand accepts it too.

exercises.guide: Give the root a flag every command shares and `serve` a flag only it accepts.

chunks.guide: `env` is persistent on the root. `port` is a plain local flag of `serve`.

exercises.guide: `env` must work on every command. `port` is only for `serve`. Fill the two gaps that make that true.

exercises.guide: Pick where the flag is accepted.
options: On the root and on serve
Nowhere, it needs a Run function
exercises.explanation: `Flags()` makes a local flag: only the command that owns it accepts it. Subcommands inherit only what is added with `PersistentFlags()`.

exercises.title: Flag before the subcommand
exercises.guide: The program runs as `go run main.go --env prod serve`.
exercises.explanation: A persistent flag is accepted before or after the subcommand, so `env` is set to `prod` before `serve` runs.

slides.text: A persistent flag travels down, never up and never sideways: it reaches the commands under the one that owns it. A command can read an inherited flag from its own flag set, by name.

exercises.title: A flag for one branch
exercises.guide: Put a persistent flag on `db`: its `migrate` subcommand inherits it.

chunks.guide: `db` owns the flag. It is persistent, so it reaches the commands below `db`.

notes.text: Reaches db and its subcommands, not the root.

chunks.guide: Nest `migrate` under `db`, and `db` under the root.

exercises.title: Who accepts --dry-run?
exercises.guide: Pick the commands that accept the flag.
exercises.explanation: A persistent flag reaches the command that owns it and everything below it. `serve` is a sibling of `db` and the root is above it.

exercises.guide: Read an inherited flag from inside `Run` with its name, without a variable.

exercises.title: The root reads it too
exercises.guide: The root has a `Run` of its own. Fill the gaps so it reads its string flag `name` by name, and declares that flag as persistent, so every subcommand shares it.

exercises.title: Flag added after AddCommand
exercises.guide: The program runs as `go run main.go serve --env prod`.
exercises.explanation: Inherited flags are collected when the command runs, so it does not matter that `env` was added after `AddCommand`.
